pools.displayName: Windows 11 with Smart App Control on
pools.purpose: Prove that an official signed installer and installed binaries remain trusted and runnable when Smart App Control is enforcing reputation policy.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Confirm that Smart App Control is in enforcement state before installation.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record the numeric policy state with the Windows edition, version, and OS build.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Verify the exact official installer selected for the run.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record signature status and public signer subject without certificate private material.

authoritativeCommands.command: Install $env:OPENCLAW_PROOF_INSTALLER, launch OpenClaw Companion from the installed location, and exercise first-run navigation.
authoritativeCommands.purpose: Exercise the reputation-sensitive install and process launch path.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Capture installer exit status plus a screenshot showing the installed app running and any Smart App Control decision.

collect: Windows edition, version, OS build, and Smart App Control policy state
installer SHA-256, signature status, and public signer subject
installer exit status and consented screenshots of trust decisions or the running app
redact: Windows user name, machine name, and user-profile paths
notification content, recent files, and unrelated desktop applications
neverCollect: certificate private keys or signing credentials
gateway tokens, setup codes, device identities, or environment variable dumps
unreviewed full-desktop recordings

requiredWhen: release signing, installer identity, executable layout, or reputation behavior changes
a release candidate must claim Smart App Control compatibility
doesNotProve: unsigned local installers are accepted by Smart App Control
gateway, MXC, GPU, or upgrade behavior

pools.purpose: Prove Gateway to Windows node system.run containment through a real WSL Gateway on a host where MXC and AppContainer execute rather than skip.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Run the formal Gateway to Windows node MXC proof and fail if a required proof skips.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Publish the redacted console log, TRX summary, and the three named proof outcomes.

collect: test names, pass counts, exit codes, duration, and MXC containment markers
redacted isolated-run logs and TRX files under TestResults\MxcE2E
Windows, WSL, architecture, and MXC availability versions
redact: Windows user name, machine name, temporary paths, and WSL user name
command output that contains user content or host-specific paths
neverCollect: gateways.json, settings.json, device identity files, or raw approval stores
gateway tokens, setup codes, private keys, or raw command environment
an AllowSkip result presented as merge proof

requiredWhen: MXC sandboxing, system.run, exec approvals, or Windows command execution changes
gateway setup or connection changes can alter the MXC execution path
doesNotProve: a hosted-runner skip is MXC coverage
installer, Smart App Control, ARM64, GPU, or visual UI behavior

pools.purpose: Prove native ARM64 build, packaging dependencies, launch, WebView2, and representative tray behavior on ARM64 Windows hardware.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Build the native ARM64 tray payload on ARM64 Windows.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record the build exit code, architecture, and warning/error summary.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Launch the current native tray build with isolated state.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Capture process architecture and consented screenshots of the tray, Settings, and a WebView2-backed surface.

collect: OS build, PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE, runtime identifier, build result, and process architecture
native dependency presence and public signature metadata for official payloads
consented screenshots of representative native and WebView2 surfaces
redact: Windows user name, machine name, user-profile paths, and unrelated tray icons
gateway endpoints, session names, and user-authored chat content
neverCollect: gateway tokens, setup codes, private keys, or device identity files
full environment dumps or unrelated desktop screenshots
x64 emulation results presented as native ARM64 proof

requiredWhen: native dependencies, runtime identifiers, WebView2, architecture-specific packaging, or ARM64 behavior changes
a release candidate must make a native ARM64 runtime claim
doesNotProve: GitHub ARM64 compilation alone proves interactive runtime behavior
DGX, Blackwell, MXC, Smart App Control, or upgrade behavior

pools.displayName: Windows and WSL with DGX or Blackwell GPU
pools.purpose: Prove local AI GPU detection, setup, restart, and representative inference against a WSL-visible NVIDIA DGX or Blackwell device.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Confirm that the selected WSL distro can see the expected DGX or Blackwell GPU.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record GPU model and driver version only.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Run focused local AI GPU setup and restart policy tests before hardware proof.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Publish the nonzero test count, exit status, and local-ai-gpu.trx.

authoritativeCommands.command: Use isolated tray state to install or select the local AI provider, restart its managed runtime, and send a fixed non-sensitive prompt.
authoritativeCommands.purpose: Prove the current build reaches real GPU-backed inference after setup and restart.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Capture redacted provider status, model identifier, bounded response timing, and GPU utilization summary.

collect: GPU product name, driver version, WSL version, model identifier, and coarse utilization
focused test counts, setup outcome, restart outcome, and bounded inference timing
redacted diagnostics from isolated tray and WSL state
redact: GPU UUID, serial number, machine name, WSL user, and user-profile paths
model prompts and responses except the fixed reviewed proof prompt
neverCollect: API keys, model service credentials, gateway tokens, setup codes, or private keys
nvidia-smi process lists, full environment dumps, or arbitrary local model content
CPU fallback presented as DGX or Blackwell GPU proof

requiredWhen: local AI GPU detection, GPU setup, managed model routing, or GPU restart behavior changes
a release candidate must claim DGX or Blackwell compatibility
doesNotProve: mocked GPU unit tests are hardware inference proof
generic ARM64, MXC, Smart App Control, installer, or gateway pairing behavior

pools.purpose: Prove clean install, previous-version upgrade, current-version repair, and uninstall behavior with exact official artifacts on a restorable Windows host.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Bind the run to two exact signed installer artifacts.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record file names, SHA-256 values, versions, signature status, and public signer subject.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Run current installer source, payload, cleanup, identity, and protocol assertions.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Publish the nonzero test count, exit status, and installer-source.trx.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Verify signing policy against the payload installed from the new official artifact.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record the verifier result and public signer metadata.

authoritativeCommands.command: Restore the clean snapshot, install $env:OPENCLAW_PROOF_OLD_INSTALLER, seed only reviewed non-secret settings, install $env:OPENCLAW_PROOF_NEW_INSTALLER, launch, repair, uninstall, and verify expected preserved and removed state.
authoritativeCommands.purpose: Exercise stateful upgrade behavior that source assertions do not cover.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Capture artifact hashes, exit codes, version transitions, expected state assertions, and consented first-run or upgrade screenshots.

collect: artifact file names, versions, SHA-256 values, signature status, exit codes, and installer assertion results
explicit assertions for expected preserved settings and removed files
consented screenshots of clean first run and post-upgrade app version
redact: Windows user name, machine name, user-profile paths, and installed unrelated software
gateway endpoints and any seeded settings not required by the reviewed scenario
neverCollect: real user AppData, gateway records, tokens, setup codes, device identities, or private keys
signing credentials, certificate private material, or release environment variables
an unsigned local installer presented as official release proof

requiredWhen: installer, updater, file layout, setup prerequisites, state migration, repair, or uninstall behavior changes
a release candidate must claim clean install or upgrade compatibility
doesNotProve: installer source assertions alone prove upgrade preservation
gateway, MXC, GPU, Smart App Control, or native ARM64 behavior

pools.purpose: Prove product-owned WSL Gateway setup, bootstrap, operator pairing, Windows node pairing, and representative Gateway invocation.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Run the current real WSL Gateway setup, bootstrap, pairing, and node invocation E2E class.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Publish the nonzero test count, gateway-setup-connect.trx, and redacted loopback diagnostics emitted by the E2E run.

collect: exact Gateway and Node versions, protocol version, test outcomes, and pairing state names
gateway-setup-connect.trx, aggregate test counts, and redacted loopback-only network diagnostics
representative command name, status, and duration without arguments or payload
redact: Windows and WSL user names, machine name, user-profile paths, and gateway record identifiers
session names, command arguments, response content, and endpoint details beyond loopback port
neverCollect: setup codes, bootstrap or device tokens, private keys, gateways.json, or settings.json
raw QR payloads, device identity files, or arbitrary command output
PreflightOnly or a skipped pairing stage presented as complete Gateway proof

requiredWhen: WSL Gateway setup, bootstrap, pairing, reconnect, recovery, protocol, or Gateway-mediated node behavior changes
a Gateway release candidate is promoted for Windows compatibility
doesNotProve: unit tests or local MCP invocation prove the real Gateway path
MXC containment unless windows-wsl-mxc also runs
installer, Smart App Control, GPU, ARM64, or visual acceptance

pools.purpose: Collect current-head visible proof for changed tray, Settings, onboarding, chat, canvas, Command Center, accessibility, or permission behavior.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Launch the current worktree build without mutating real tray settings.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Record the commit, isolated data directory class, process start result, and consented screenshots of the changed state.

authoritativeCommands.purpose: Run the existing real-process accessibility quality gate for UI changes.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Publish the nonzero test count, winui-accessibility.trx, and Axe finding summaries.

authoritativeCommands.command: Use computer-use against the isolated current-head app to exercise the changed path and capture only the relevant app window.
authoritativeCommands.purpose: Show the active changed state rather than an adjacent or empty UI.
authoritativeCommands.evidence: Attach focused screenshots or video with exact reproduction steps and observed result.

collect: current commit, OS build, app version, exact reproduction steps, and accessibility summary
focused screenshots or video of the OpenClaw app window with user consent
redacted UI diagnostics containing state names, counts, and coarse error categories
redact: user-authored chat, session titles, gateway endpoints, Windows user name, and machine name
unrelated windows, desktop notifications, tray icons, and user-profile paths
neverCollect: tokens, setup codes, private keys, device identities, raw settings, or gateway files
full-desktop capture when an app-window capture is sufficient
screenshots from a different commit presented as current-head proof

requiredWhen: tray, Settings, onboarding, chat, canvas, Command Center, permissions, diagnostics, or accessibility behavior changes
automated tests cannot directly show the user-visible changed state
doesNotProve: a screenshot alone proves Gateway, MCP, installer, MXC, GPU, or ARM64 behavior
unit tests alone are visual acceptance
